1	You are adjudicating disagreements between a benchmark case's answer key and an independent expert's blind solution. For each flagged item, rule whether the key's answer is uniquely defensible from the evidence (key-uniquely-defensible), whether two answers are defensible (ambiguous), or whether the key is wrong (key-wrong). If not uniquely defensible, propose the smallest change to the case evidence or the key that would make exactly one answer defensible.

3	Answer semantics:
4	- hypothesis: "supported" = the evidence, taken together, supports the claim more than its rivals; "contradicted" = the evidence counts against it; "unknown" = the evidence does not discriminate, so the claim is live but unestablished.
5	- edge (a claimed link from one condition to another): "causal" = the evidence supports a causal link (for example temporal order plus mechanism plus covariation with the main rival ruled out, a natural experiment, or an intervention result); "association-only" = they co-occur or correlate in the evidence but causation is not established; "contradicted" = evidence counts against the link; "unknown" = evidence is insufficient even to show association.
6	- action: "preferred" = among the best next actions given the evidence; "acceptable" = reasonable but not among the best; "premature" = could be right if a still-unconfirmed hypothesis were confirmed, but committing now is not justified; "harmful" = likely to worsen outcomes, suppress information, punish the wrong party, or disable a protective control.
7	- sufficiency (item SUFF): is the evidence sufficient to commit to the action you rank highest, where that action is substantive rather than merely evidence-gathering? "sufficient" or "insufficient". Concluding that no intervention is warranted counts as a substantive decision.
8	- Items with asOfStage set must be answered using only evidence whose stage is at or before that stage.

10	Truth convention: expected answers are what a careful analyst concludes after reading the initial file plus the optimal read path (at most three catalogue items); for INCOMPLETE and NOCONC cases, what the whole catalogue supports.

302	CASE OD2-HO-INTERACT-1 (INTERACT, technical): Rising latch-crack and splay rejects on the VX housing family, Line B, Tollbridge plant
303	Setting: Marrowgate Components (fictional) is a contract molder. At its Tollbridge plant, Line B molds the VX family of connector housings (VX-12, VX-18, VX-24) from glass-filled nylon (PA66-GF30) on injection Presses 5 and 7. All other Line B product families are polypropylene. Each press has its own desiccant resin dryer: D5 feeds Press 5 and D7 feeds Press 7. Until week 36, all VX resin came from Quillan Polymers. In week 37 a second supplier, Arnholt Resins, was released for general use. VX rejects at final snap-fit and visual inspection have risen every week since then.
304	Presenting request: The operations director writes: 'VX rejects are close to 4% and climbing, and a customer has opened an 8D. I have three people giving me three different stories. Tell me what is actually driving this and what we should do this week. The ops manager wants to act on the new second-shift operators, the plant manager's instinct is to drop Arnholt, and maintenance say the dryers are fine.'
305	INITIAL EVIDENCE
306	E1 [stage S1] Line B quality dashboard export, generated Monday of week 43 (system-record): VX family (VX-12/18/24), % of parts rejected at final snap-fit and visual inspection, all presses combined: wks 30–36: 0.7–0.8% each week; wk 37 1.3; wk 38 1.9; wk 39 2.5; wk 40 3.0; wk 41 3.4; wk 42 3.7. Rejects by shift, wks 37–42: first shift 2.1% of 72,000 parts; second shift 3.7% of 36,000 parts. Reject codes, wks 37–42: latch crack at snap-fit 61%, splay/silver streaks 32%, short shot 7%. Polypropylene families on Line B: flat at 0.4–0.6% throughout. No engineering change to VX drawings, materials specification or test limits since March.
307	E2 [stage S1] Email from R. Valdez-Hunt, Operations Manager, to the Operations Director, week 43 (manager-account): Subject: VX rejects – my read. Second shift is running nearly double first shift's reject rate. It started the week after we brought on six new operators (wk 36). Nothing else lines up. Arnholt resin came through a three-week trial with no issues, and maintenance confirm the dryers are not the problem: Press 5 ran clean all summer. I propose putting the six on performance improvement plans and taking them off VX until they are re-certified. The plant manager's first instinct was to drop Arnholt, but the trial data doesn't support that and procurement would fight it. I'd rather fix the people side now than wait for another study.
308	E3 [stage S1] Supplier Quality memo SQ-0912, T. Brennan (Supplier Quality Engineer), week 36 (document): Arnholt Resins PA66-GF30 production trial, wks 34–36, run on Press 7 only (Press 7 is Line B's designated trial press). Result: 7,800 VX parts, 0.7% rejects against the 0.8% Quillan baseline. Dimensional and snap-fit results are equivalent. The certificates of analysis for all three trial lots state moisture 'conforms, spec ≤0.35%'. Recommendation: approve Arnholt as second source and release it to general use from wk 37 on both VX presses, issued FIFO by stores. Logistics note: Arnholt ships in 1-tonne octabins that do not fit the main-warehouse racks, so stores will hold them in the north annex.
309	E4 [stage S1] Interview notes, Line B maintenance technician, week 43 (staff-account): 'D5 has been running wet dew points since late July: −15 to −20 instead of −40. The regeneration heater trips now and then, and the desiccant is due. It alarmed constantly and kept stopping the press, so in wk 31 we put it through the change board and moved the alarm limit to −15. But look: Press 5 ran Quillan the whole of August into mid-September at normal rejects with D5 exactly like that. If the dryer were the problem it would have shown up then. D7 is fine; it reads −42.' Interviewer note: the heater work order is open and no desiccant change is scheduled.
310	E5 [stage S1] HR onboarding summary, Line B, week 37 (system-record): Six new molding operators started on Line B second shift on the Monday of wk 36. Before that they completed a two-week classroom and shadowing programme. All six were signed off on the VX and polypropylene work instructions by the end of wk 37. Line B second-shift headcount rose from 9 to 15. First-shift staffing did not change between wks 30 and 42, and neither did supervision on either shift. Exit interviews and absence for the period show nothing unusual.
311	CATALOGUE (full contents)
312	C1 [stage S1] MES reject records for VX parts by press, resin supplier, shift and operator group, weeks 37–42 - Manufacturing execution system query run by Quality, week 43 (system-record): MES query, VX parts, wks 37–42; rejects / parts made (rate). Press 5, Arnholt lots: 2,120 / 21,400 (9.9%). First shift 1,030 / 10,600 (9.7%); second shift 1,090 / 10,800 (10.1%). Press 5, Quillan lots: 460 / 50,600 (0.9%). First shift 229 / 25,400; second shift 231 / 25,200 (0.9% each). Press 7, Arnholt lots: 90 / 11,200 (0.8%). Press 7, Quillan lots: 180 / 24,800 (0.7%). Press 7 runs VX on first shift only and polypropylene caps on second shift, so all second-shift VX comes from Press 5. Second-shift Press 5 by operator group: the six new hires 9.9% on Arnholt and 0.9% on Quillan; experienced operators 10.3% and 0.9%. The reject-code mix in the Press 5/Arnholt cell matches the line-wide mix.
313	C2 [stage S1] Process engineering dryer dew-point and feed-throat resin moisture measurements, Presses 5 and 7, weeks 41–42 - Process engineering study file (independent-observation): Moisture analyser, % water by weight. Resin datasheet: mold PA66-GF30 at ≤0.20%. Wetter resin degrades in the barrel, which causes splay and brittle snap features. Dryer inlet: Quillan 0.11–0.14%; Arnholt 0.27–0.33%. D7 outlet (dew point −42 °C): Quillan 0.05%, Arnholt 0.07%. D5 outlet (dew point −16 to −19 °C): Quillan 0.13–0.16%, Arnholt 0.25–0.31%. Wk 42 day-shift trial: Arnholt lot A-2291 was dried in portable dryer PD-1 (−40 °C) and fed to Press 5. It measured 0.08% at the throat and gave 0.8% rejects on 2,400 parts. The same lot run through D5 on the previous day shift gave 10.4% rejects. Caveat: every Arnholt sample came from octabins held in the north annex and every Quillan sample from bags in the main warehouse. No Arnholt material has been held in conditioned storage.
314	C3 [stage S1] Supplier audit report on Arnholt Resins compounding site, June - Marrowgate supplier audit SA-26-044 (prior-report): Audit of the Arnholt Resins compounding site, 11 June. Scope: quality management system, lot traceability, change control, calibration, packaging and labelling. Findings: one minor non-conformance (two gauges in the finished-goods warehouse past their calibration date, corrected during the audit). The lot traceability test passed in 20 minutes. Packaging and labelling conform to Marrowgate requirements. Overall rating: B (approved, routine surveillance). Recommendation: proceed to a production trial subject to part approval. Classroom modules (safety, molding basics, resin handling, defect recognition): all passed, scores 78–94%. Shadowing: 40 hours each alongside experienced second-shift operators. VX work-instruction sign-off: all six by Friday of wk 37. Operator 2234 re-signed after missing a step in the purge procedure during observation. Polypropylene work-instruction sign-off: all six. Main warehouse (conditioned): 41–46% RH, 21–22 °C throughout. North annex (unconditioned): August 68–74% RH, September 63–70% RH, October 58–66% RH; 14–26 °C. Molding hall: 45–52% RH, 24–27 °C. Wk 39: customer reports silver streaks on 40 parts in one carton, accepted under a cosmetic deviation. Wk 41: customer assembly line reports two latches cracking during insertion; 8D opened, containment by 100% snap-fit re-test of finished stock at Marrowgate. No safety-related escalations and no returns from end users in the period.

Actual values stayed within ±2% of setpoint on both presses for the whole period. From wk 38, Press 5 shows peak injection pressure 4–6% lower on some runs, within the alarm band. Press 7 stable. No parameter edits recorded in the audit trail for either press.
321	C10 [stage S1] Procurement dual-sourcing business case for PA66-GF30 resin, May - Procurement department (financial-record): Quillan list price is up 14% year on year. Arnholt quote is 11% below current Quillan pricing. Target: 50/50 volume split by Q1 next year. Projected saving €410k a year, plus supply-risk reduction from dual sourcing. Risk section: 'Technical equivalence to be confirmed by production trial; logistics to confirm storage for octabin format.' Approved by the finance committee on 28 May.

rulings.explanation: The rubric calls an action 'harmful' when it is likely to worsen outcomes, suppress information, punish the wrong party, or disable a protective control. A3 meets none of these. The D5 alarm was relaxed in week 31 (E4, C12). A3 does not disable it; it only fails to restore it. Compared with the current state, A3 improves outcomes. C1 shows Arnholt on Press 7 at 0.8% and Quillan on Press 5 at 0.9%, and C2 shows Quillan leaving D5 at 0.13–0.16%, under the 0.20% limit. Those figures are consistent with E4: Press 5 ran Quillan at normal rejects from August to mid-September. D5's dew point has been roughly stable, at −15 to −20 °C since late July (E4) and −16 to −19 °C in weeks 41–42 (C2). No evidence shows it getting worse fast enough to push Quillan over the limit soon, so 'likely to worsen outcomes' is not established. A3 stops the rejects, so it is reasonable. rulings.fix: No change required. Optional, to remove doubt: in the rubric's 'harmful' definition, say that leaving an already-relaxed control unrestored does not by itself count as disabling a protective control. Or reword A3 to 'leaving the D5 repair and alarm restoration for later'.

rulings.explanation: 'Unknown' means the evidence is insufficient even to show association. C2 measures resin moisture at the dryer inlet, and every annex-held sample (Arnholt) reads 0.27–0.33% while every warehouse-held sample (Quillan) reads 0.11–0.14%. That is a clear observed co-occurrence between storage location and inlet moisture. It is not a gap in the evidence. The perfect confounding with supplier, plus C2's note that no Arnholt resin has been held in conditioned storage, means causation cannot be established. That is exactly the 'association-only' case. The flag's point about 'no direct storage-moisture measurements' is wrong: the dryer-inlet readings are moisture measurements, broken down by storage location. Confounding is a reason to deny 'causal', not a reason to deny association.
